mission: The Existential Risk Observatory is a Dutch nonprofit founded by physicist Otto Barten that believes awareness is the first step to reducing existential risk. It informs the public debate through media work, events and message-testing research, with a focus on unaligned AI. Its policy research now centres on international agreements to halt frontier AI development and how they could be verified.

key_work.title: How to Catch a GPU: A Taxonomy of Verification and Enforcement Mechanisms for International AI Agreements
key_work.plain_summary: Catalogues the ways an international AI treaty could be checked and enforced — mainly by tracking and controlling AI chips.

key_work.title: Trends in Public Attitude Towards Existential Risk and Artificial Intelligence
key_work.plain_summary: Tracks how public awareness and concern about AI existential risk have changed over time.

warnings.text: Existential risk has risen from almost zero to an estimated one in six this century (citing Toby Ord's The Precipice) — unacceptably high.
Future AI with goals different from ours (unaligned AI) is the leading existential risk.
These risks are neglected partly because the public is not aware of them.

recommendations.text: Inform the public debate — awareness is the first step to reducing existential risk.
A conditional international AI safety treaty that halts frontier development when danger thresholds are reached.
Build verification and enforcement mechanisms, especially for AI chips, so such agreements can work.
